Consulter
kon-SUL-ter
noun
From the Latin consultare, “to take counsel.” The AV’s “consulter with familiar spirits” is not a modern adviser but the client of the occult — the one who goes to a medium to seek counsel from demons.

Biblical Definition

The consulter is the client of the occult — not the medium who owns the familiar spirit, but the man who comes to her for counsel. The word is the Latin consultare, “to take counsel,” and the modern reader who hears only a harmless adviser must recover the AV’s dark sense: the consulter seeks the seance, and the law warns that the guilt is not the practitioner’s alone but his. Saul is the great and terrible example. The chronicler writes his epitaph plainly: “Saul died… for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it” (1Ch 10:13) — the crowning sin of a wasted reign was that he consulted a demon rather than his God, and enquired not of the LORD. He had said, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her” (1Sa 28:7), and that errand was his death. Isaiah presses the folly on every would-be consulter: when men urge you to “seek unto them that have familiar spirits… should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead?” (Isa 8:19). And the LORD Himself vows to hunt the consulter down: “the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits… I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people” (Lev 20:6). To consult the dead is to abandon the living God.

Webster 1828 Definition

One who consults familiar spirits — the client of the medium, guilty with the diviner he seeks.

CONSULTER, one who consults; in the AV, one that seeks counsel of familiar spirits.

From Latin consultare, “to take counsel,” but here counsel sought from demons.

The consulter is the client, not the practitioner, yet shares the guilt of the art.

Saul died for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit (1Ch 10:13).

The LORD sets His face against the soul that turns to familiar spirits (Lev 20:6).

Key Scripture

1Ch 10:13 — "So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD, even against the word of the LORD, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it;"

1Sa 28:7 — "Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at Endor."

Isa 8:19 — "And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep, and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead?"

Lev 20:6 — "And the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits, and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people."

Modern Corruption

The consulter is not extinct but multiplied — every client of the psychic, the medium, the tarot reader, and the astrologer app is a consulter with familiar spirits, and shares the guilt.

expand to see more

The living corruption here is that the occult client-base has never been larger, and never felt more innocent. The consulter is the one who buys the reading, books the seance, downloads the astrology app, texts the psychic hotline, orders the tarot spread — who does not practise the art but seeks its counsel. Modern conscience excuses him easily: he is only curious, only entertained, only comforted. But Scripture lays the guilt squarely on the seeker as well as the seer. Saul did not own a familiar spirit; he consulted one, and it is named the sin that killed him. To seek counsel from the dark is to forsake the God who commands us to seek Him.

The remedy is the God who welcomes every honest seeker to Himself. “Should not a people seek unto their God?” (Isa 8:19) — the door He forbids to the medium He throws open to prayer. The consulter is condemned not for wanting counsel but for wanting it from a forbidden source; the same longing, turned to the throne of grace, is welcomed and answered. The LORD who set His face against the soul that turned to familiar spirits (Lev 20:6) sets His face in favour on the soul that turns to Him. Saul consulted a demon and died; the believer consults his God in Christ and lives.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word is consultare, “to take counsel” — the AV consulter seeks counsel of familiar spirits, and shares their guilt.

expand to see more

Consulter — from Latin consultare, “to take counsel.”

In the AV it is short for a “consulter with familiar spirits” — the medium’s client.

The guilt falls on the seeker as well as the practitioner (1Ch 10:13).

Saul consulted a familiar spirit at Endor and died for it (1Sa 28:7).

The LORD sets His face against the soul that turns to such workers (Lev 20:6).

Usage

"A consulter is the client of the occult — Saul consulted a familiar spirit, and it is called the sin that slew him."

"The word is consultare, to take counsel; the AV consulter takes his counsel from demons."

"Every customer of the psychic and the medium is, in the AV’s plain word, a consulter with familiar spirits."
